albums.blurb: Idris Muhammad, born Leo Morris in New Orleans, drummed behind Lou Donaldson, Roberta Flack, and the Prestige soul-jazz stable before Creed Taylor signed him to the Kudu label. Power of Soul, his third album as a leader, was cut in March 1974 at Rudy Van Gelder's studio with Bob James arranging and playing keys, Grover Washington Jr. on saxophones, Randy Brecker on trumpet, and Joe Beck on guitar. It holds just four long instrumentals, opening with a version of Jimi Hendrix's title tune and closing with Washington's ten-minute "Loran's Dance."
albums.reception: AllMusic's Thom Jurek called the album "one of the reasons that Idris Muhammad is regarded as the drumming king of groove."

albums.blurb: Benny Sings is the Dutch singer-producer Tim van Berkestijn, whose feather-light take on late-'70s AM pop has made him a frequent collaborator of Rex Orange County and Free Nationals. Young Hearts, his eighth album and third for Stones Throw after City Pop and Music, was the first he handed to a single outside producer: Kenny Beats, who wraps the jazzy chord changes in bubblier electronic grooves across a brisk ten-track, 25-minute run that includes the Remi Wolf duet "Pyjamas."
albums.reception: AllMusic's review judged that the Kenny Beats collaboration takes the sunny retro-pop vibe Sings had cultivated on past albums "to another level."

albums.blurb: Terry Callier was a Chicago singer-guitarist who grew up alongside Curtis Mayfield and Jerry Butler and spent his career fusing folk, jazz, and soul into something none of those labels quite covers. What Color Is Love is the second of the three albums he made for Cadet with producer-arranger Charles Stepney, who set Callier's fingerpicking and gospel-deep voice against sweeping orchestral charts. The records sold poorly and Callier left music for computer programming, until London's acid-jazz DJs rediscovered him in the '90s and pulled him back on stage.
albums.reception: AllMusic rates the album five stars, describing it as a "musical kaleidoscope" that defies all categories, and after nearly two decades out of print on vinyl it was reissued by Verve/UMe in 2018.
